t: You're looking at the home of the British Library of Political and Economic Science, better known as the LSE Library. It's the main library of the London School of Economics, and one of the largest in the world devoted to the economic and social sciences. Around five thousand students and staff come through each day. It sits in the Lionel Robbins Building, named for the economist who led the school and shaped how economics is defined. The architect Norman Foster designed the library, and he's one of the defining names of British modernism.
